steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Sift together flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.

Cream together butter, sugar, and brown sugar in a large bowl. Mix in vanilla extract and cocoa powder, then add peanut butter, and stir until smooth. Gradually mix in the sifted ingredients until well blended. Pour milk into dough, and stir until fully combined.
Drop dough by heaping teaspoons onto ungreased baking sheets. Bake in the preheated oven until edges are lightly browned, 11 to 13 minutes. For a crunchier cookie, bake an additional minute or two.

raw_recipe.headline: Eggless Chocolate Peanut Butter Cookies
raw_recipe.description: You'd never know that these decadent chocolate peanut butter cookies are made without eggs.
raw_recipe.name: Eggless Chocolate Peanut Butter Cookies

review.reviewBody: I only made 1/2 a batch of these cookies and i made a few changes. I added 1/2 a cup of root beer instead of milk, more peanut butter then called for and the chunky kind, all sugar was brown and I added about 1/2 cup of peanut butter chips. After they cooled and I tasted one I freaked out because I could have eaten a whole batch to myself! They were so so so good! I will be making these again for sure! If using my adjustments on your recipe, keep in mind that i only made a 1/2 batch , you would need to double my adjustments.

I had to control the size a bit, for I wanted smaller cookies rather than what I got by dropping a heaping teaspoon. The second pan was the right size. While I agree the peanut butter didn't seem to add much to the flavor, my husband suggested I add a cream center and make sandwich cookies. So, I creamed together some butter, milk, and vanilla and added confectioners' sugar until I had a creamy consistency thick enough to sit between two of the cookies and had a hit!

I needed an eggless recipe for Valentine's Day treats and I had to make a couple of last minute changes: I used 6 Tbsp. cocoa powder for richer chocolate flavor and SIFTED with dry ingredients, also about 1/2 C. creamy peanut butter was pretty good, and here is a trick for super moistness and a bit of tang: place 1/4 C. sour cream in a liquid measure and add milk (this works great with water too) until it reaches the 1/2 C. mark, mix this to break up sour cream, a few small lumps is no biggie, then add alternately with dry flour mixture to creamed butter mixture, at this point I added about 3/4 C. mini M&M's and 3/4 C. semi sweet choc. chips, ROUNDED TABLESPOONFULS, baked for 13 minutes and allowed to cool about 2 minutes on the pan- these came out like moist little chocolate cakes and everyone gave the thumbs up! This is a great recipe - but don't be afraid to play around and adjust to your liking; the beauty in this one is the versatility it brings.

This cookie is amazing. I made a quarter batch to try and cooked three cookies (50 grams each) the first night with minimal chilling. Will cook the remaining three after 48 hours of chilling (I want the flavors to blend and I expect the cookie to stand up more when dough is firmer). I followed the directions almost exactly except for the following: I didn’t really cream the butter and sugar, I used unsweetened almond milk and topped with sea salt before cooking. Cooked for 9 minutes at 375f. Amazing Amazing Amazing. Pro tip: eat them so the cookie upside down, you want the sea salt to touch your tongue first.

I added a little extra peanut butter and also chocolate and peanut butter chips and was pleasantly surprised with the outcome. At first, when I checked the cookies at 11 minutes they were falling apart so I had to cook them a little extra, closer to 15 minutes but in the end they are delicious.

Somehow Christmas Eve came around and I didn't have any cookies for Santa... I scaled this recipe down to 2 servings and got 8 small cookies out of it. I was skeptical (because of no eggs and scaling down a recipe is always tricky...)! I used about 1/16 tsp each of baking soda, powder, and salt. I definitely used more cocoa powder and PB than the recipe called for, but I'm a personal fan of both :) They came out of the oven and OH MY GOSH! I wasn't really expecting to be able to taste the chocolate or PB, but it was SO GOOD! Oh, and I mixed the cocoa powder with the dry ingredients, not the butter!

Per other reviews, I doubled the cocoa and vanilla and opted to use 1 1/2 cups peanut butter and left out the butter. I also used all brown sugar. I had to add a little water to get this to incorporate but it turned out nice. Next time I will add some of the butter back in.

Came upon this recipe when I needed something sweet and had no eggs. They came out perfect! After reading reviews, I added a tbsp of cocoa powder to the dry ingredients, as well as a few dashes of cinnamon. They were the perfect sweetness for me (stuck to recommend sugar and used natural peanut butter). Will definitely make these again (even if I do have eggs)!

This recipe is great! I used 1/2 c coconut oil and 1/2 c natural peanut butter, substituted oats for the flour, omitted the brown sugar, and used almond milk instead of regular milk. Also added some white chocolate chips - these cookies are delicious! Made 2 dozen cookies with this recipe.

This was a a great eggless base for cookies. I thought It sounded a little dull so I changed it as follows: Subtituted instant choc pudding mix for the cocoa. Added two Tbls sour cream. Added all sorts of add-ins such as 1/2 cup oatmeal, 1/2 cup peanut butter chips, 1/2 cup coconuts. So amazing, don't miss the egg at all.

My son is allergic to egg whites and milk so I used 2 yolks and omitted the milk and used just a splash of water. I used homemade pb. 3 out of 4 of us loved these… the son who is allergic not so much. I baked mine for 11 minutes and let them cool because I prefer cookies soft not crunchy. They are still a little gooey but will finish cooking as they cool. I think I gained 5 lbs because I couldn't stop eating them!
Definitely a keeper! I added chocolate and peanut butter chips that made it over the top!
The best cookies I’ve ever made! That’s a keeper in my family. 🤩
OMG! these were delicious! Everyone loves them. And they never even suspect that there are no eggs. They are GREAT!!!
It’s a great recipe, I recommend it to anyone. No joke!!!
These cookies are completely flavourless. If I ever make them again, I will definitely double peanut butter and cocoa and maybe add chocolate chips. Very disappointing!
Cookies were pretty good. They came out lighter looking from your picture. I will try them again
Fine. It's healpng TBSP, not tsp to make 24. They don't taste like much, not like peanut butter or chocolate. Fluffy but disappointing, won't make again.
